University of Bristol: India | International students | University of Bristol International students Search Start searching Search Close search International students India We welcome applications from Indian students. More than 800 students from India currently study here, and we would love for you to join us. Application guidance The following information is for guidance only. Competition for places at the University of Bristol is very strong, and the achievement of a specified qualification does not guarantee that an offer will be made. We aim to respond to your application as quickly as possible to help you plan your studies. If your qualification is not mentioned or you have any further questions, please contact us for advice. Go to section Undergraduate entry requirements Postgraduate entry requirements Transferring your studies Scholarships Education representatives Student societies Our alumni Get in touch Download your Bristol Guide Get a quick introduction to the University of Bristol with our India Country Guide 2026-27 (PDF, 1,150kB) . Undergraduate entry requirements You can apply for undergraduate courses through the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (UCAS). Find out more from UCAS about applying to university in the UK . The UCAS institution code for the University of Bristol is BRISL B78 . Entry requirements vary for each course. Please check our undergraduate course listings for details of specific requirements. Applicants will need to meet the English language requirements for their chosen course. Different courses need different levels of language skills, referred to as ‘profiles’. The required profile will be shown on the course page. Find out more about our English language profiles . We understand that the majority of candidates from India have been taught in English throughout their education. CBSE or CISCE English at 70-80% or above can be accepted in lieu of another English test such as IELTS. Entry requirements for our undergraduate programmes will vary depending on the course you wish to apply for, your Year 12 examination board, and subjects taken. Typical offers for CBSE and CISCE range from 80% (equivalent to ABB at A-level) to 90% (equivalent to A*AA at A-level). If you would like advice relating to your specific qualification, please contact us . LLB Law applicants We are pleased to note that Bristol’s LLB Law degree is recognised by the Bar Council of India. Postgraduate entry requirements You should apply online for all our postgraduate programmes. Entry requirements vary for each programme. Please check our postgraduate programme listings for details of specific requirements. Applicants will need to meet the English language requirements for their chosen course. Different courses need different levels of language skills, referred to as ‘profiles’. The required profile will be shown on the course page. Find out more about our English language profiles . To be considered for admission to a master's degree programme at the University of Bristol, the minimum requirement for entry is typically an undergraduate degree from an acceptable institution that is equivalent to a UK upper second-class degree (also known as a 2:1). Qualifications from selected institutions may require accreditation. Applicants who hold a bachelor's degree from an accepted Indian university with a minimum of GPA of 6/10 or 60% will be considered for admission to a master's degree (the requirement will depend on your undergraduate university and the programme you have applied for). Applicants to our Law programmes can be considered with minimum grades of 55-60% from an accepted Indian university. Applicants who hold a first class master's degree from a prestigious university will be considered for admission to PhD study. If you would like advice relating to your specific qualification, please contact us . Applicants will be required to complete a qualification verification with our partner Qualification Check before a CAS can be issued. A link to complete the check will be sent by email once applicants have accepted an unconditional offer and made any required deposit payment . Transferring your studies The University of Bristol maintains important partnerships with a number of world-leading universities in India. If you are studying an eligible degree at one of our partner universities, you can apply to transfer your studies to Bristol through our Global Transfer Programme. Applications made via our Global Transfer Programme are processed faster using a streamlined admission route. To check whether you are eligible and how to apply, visit our Global Transfer Programme webpages . Scholarships The University provides a range of international scholarships , including our Think Big scholarships which can help fund your tuition fees. Search our full list of funding to find more scholarships offered by the University of Bristol and external organisations. Find more information about funding your studies on our student finances pages . In addition to University of Bristol scholarships, Indian students can apply for Chevening Scholarships and Commonwealth Scholarships. Other opportunities have previously included the Zutshi-Smith Scholarship for PhD students. Education representatives The University has agreements with many education representatives (also known as agents) around the world who can assist you with your application. Using a representative does not put your application at any advantage or disadvantage, and independent applications will be considered on an equal basis. Please use the services of only one representative to avoid administrative complications. We strongly advise you to only work with a representative listed below. Please note that official representatives of the University of Bristol receive a commission payment for their services supporting incoming international students. The University does not pay commission to agents representing students receiving US federal loans. If you have any complaint or feedback about your experience with our education representatives, please contact us at international-office@bristol.ac.uk . The British Council have produced an online guide for students to support you in choosing an education agent. The University works with the following agencies: AECC Global Edwise International Envision Overseas Education Fateh Education Gateway Abroad GeeBee Education IDP India International Placewell Consultants (IPC) Kavi Trivedi EduConsultants KC Overseas Education Private Limited Santa Monica Study Abroad Shiksha Study Abroad StudyIn TC Global British Council The British Council can give guidance and information about higher education in the UK. Find out from their website if there is an office near you and what services are available. Student societies Our student clubs include the Indian Society ; Asian Society , Tamil Society , Hindu Society , Bollywood Dance Society and over 400 more for different interests and hobbies. Our alumni Our international alumni community includes more than 1,000 students from or living in India, who are employed at organisations including Airbus, Amazon, Deloitte, General Electric, Jaguar Land Rover, the United Nations, the NHS and universities around the world. Get in touch The University of Bristol has a representative office (via our partner UKIBC India Pvt. University of Leeds: Entry requirements | University of Leeds Skip to main content University of Leeds homepage Search leeds.ac.uk Search all leeds.ac.uk Entry requirements To study at Leeds, you’ll need to meet the academic entry requirements for your course and have a recognised English language qualification. Course requirements Use our Course Search to find the academic and English language entry requirements for your course. Check the accepted qualifications for your country or region . If you have any questions about your qualifications, email the International Office at internationaloffice@leeds.ac.uk . English language requirements IELTS (International English Language Testing System) We specify English language requirements in terms of IELTS. We accept both IELTS Academic and IELTS for UKVI (United Kingdom Visas and Immigration) (Academic). The test must be taken at a test centre. We cannot accept results from an IELTS test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single IELTS test, or via a single test and One Skill Retake. We also accept a range of other English language qualifications, which are listed in the next section. Minimum requirements by study level The following are the minimum English language requirements for each level of study. Some of our courses have higher English language requirements. Check the entry requirements for your course via Course Search or, for postgraduate research programmes, the relevant faculty graduate school website. We offer pre-sessional English courses to improve your academic English language level and help you prepare for study in the UK. You may be able to use a pre-sessional to meet the English language requirement for your course. International Foundation Year See the English language requirements for our International Foundation Year . Undergraduate degrees IELTS Academic or IELTS for UKVI (Academic): 6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in each component. TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test): 80 overall with no less than 18 in reading, 17 in listening, 20 in speaking and 19 in writing (for tests taken before 21 January 2026) or 4 overall with no less than 4 in each component (for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026). We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single TOEFL iBT test taken in a test centre. We do not accept TOEFL MyBest scores or the TOEFL iBT Paper Edition. PTE (Pearson Test of English) Academic or PTE Academic UKVI: 60 overall with no less than 59 in each component. We cannot accept results from these tests that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. We do not accept PTE Academic Online. LanguageCert Academic or LanguageCert Academic SELT (Secure English Language Test): 65 overall with no less than 60 in each component. We cannot accept results from these tests that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. The test must have been taken in a test centre. Oxford ELLT (English Language Level Test) Global: 6 overall with no less than 5 in each component. We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. Oxford Test of English Advanced: 126 overall with no less than 111 in each component. We accept results from the full test of all four components or from individual tests of each component. We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. A suitable Cambridge English qualification: 169 overall with no less than 162 in each component. The grade that you need for your course will determine which qualification you should take: B1 Preliminary, B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency. Check which qualification is relevant to your required grade on the Cambridge English website. Trinity College London ISE (Integrated Skills in English): Pass in ISE II or above. We cannot accept results from this test that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. NCUK English for Academic Purposes (EAP): C overall with no less than D in each component. We cannot usually accept results from this test that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. NCUK English for Academic Purposes for Proficient Users (EAPPU): C overall with no less than D in each component. We cannot usually accept results from this test that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. Study Group Academic English Skills (AES): 60% overall with no less than 50% in each component. GCSE English Language or IGCSE English as a First or Second Language: C or 4. GCSE English Literature may be considered in certain circumstances for some courses. A-level or AS-level English Language or English Literature: C. National 5 English: C. Scottish Higher or Advanced Higher English Language or English Literature: C. AP (Advanced Placement) English Language and Composition or English Literature and Composition: 3. IB (International Baccalaureate): English A (first language) Literature or Language and Literature – 4 at higher level (HL) or 4 at standard level (SL). English B (second language) – 5 at HL or 6 at SL. English B is not accepted at SL for courses with an IELTS requirement of 7.0 or above. English Literature and Performance and English Ab Initio are not accepted. A minimum of two years of study in the UK to complete an undergraduate degree. A minimum of two years of study at a Russell Group university’s overseas campus to complete an undergraduate degree where the medium of instruction was English. For overseas doctors registered with the NHS, we will accept this as evidence of your English language ability for courses requiring an IELTS up to 6.5 overall. For courses with a higher requirement, acceptance will be at the discretion of the course admissions team. We may accept an English language qualification from your country, which you can find among our international admissions qualifications . Masters degrees IELTS Academic or IELTS for UKVI (Academic): 6.5 overall with no less than 6.0 in each component. TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test): 88 overall with no less than 20 in reading, 19 in listening, 22 in speaking and 21 in writing (for tests taken before 21 January 2026) or 4.5 overall with no less than 4 in reading, listening and speaking and 4.5 in writing (for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026). We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. You must meet the requirements through a single TOEFL iBT test taken in a test centre. We do not accept TOEFL MyBest scores or the TOEFL iBT Paper Edition. PTE (Pearson Test of English) Academic or PTE Academic UKVI: 64 overall with no less than 60 in each component. We cannot accept results from these tests that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. We do not accept PTE Academic Online. LanguageCert Academic or LanguageCert Academic SELT (Secure English Language Test): 70 overall with no less than 65 in each component. We cannot accept results from these tests that are over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. The test must have been taken in a test centre. Oxford ELLT (English Language Level Test) Global: 7 overall with no less than 6 in each component. We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old at the start date of the course you intend to study. Oxford Test of English Advanced: 140 overall with no less than 126 in each component. We accept results from the full test of all four components or from individual tests of each component. We cannot accept results from a test that is over two years old
